protocol: Alternating A/B/A/B. Each pass: navigate, 15 s warm-up discarded, counters reset, 30 s steady-state window, n=240 GPU timestamp samples. Measured with training stopped so nothing else held a Metal context.

summary.verdict: No cost difference is resolvable from two paired passes. The candidate deploys a bit-identical graph shape, both models held every gate, and the between-model differences are the same size as the production model's own variation between its two passes. Two passes per model is too few to bound a sub-millisecond difference, and no such bound is claimed.
summary.spreadComparison: Pairwise candidate-minus-production p50 differences are -0.070 and +0.320 ms. The production model's own run-to-run spread is 0.220 ms, so the first pair sits inside it and the second does not. Only the mean difference, 0.125 ms, is smaller than that spread.

candidate: models/m7-final/R3-seed12.json (selected final seed), served as /models/m7-r3-candidate.json during measurement
timingScope: GPU timestamp bracket that opens at ingest and closes at our own present/blit. It spans the whole upscale stage - every neural compute pass plus the pipeline ingest and present brackets - on the importExternalTexture path, and excludes video decode and the browser's own compositing. Our code adds no separate upload pass there, but whether the browser copied internally was not observable.
discardedAttempt: An earlier attempt on the same day was discarded and is not reported as a measurement. It ran while final-seed training held the MPS context: both second passes fell back to the Catmull-Rom scaler, and the sample windows were unequal (n=39 against n=240). Recorded here because why a number was discarded is worth more than the number was.
samplingScope: n=240 is the trailing window the stats ring buffer retains, not every frame in the pass. Each 30 s pass rendered about 1,750 frames; the reported percentiles describe the last 240 of them, after a discarded 15 s warm-up.

gpuMemory.why: WebGPU exposes no device or process memory query to JavaScript, and the production pipeline carries no memory instrumentation. Reporting a device-level figure would mean inventing one.

allocationComputedFromSites.derivation: Computed from the allocation sites in src/core/upscale/neural-upscaler.ts:198-262, not read back from the device. Every size there depends only on source dimensions, model features, depth and precision.

gpuMemory.parityArgument: Structural and limited to requested resources. The candidate and the shipped model have identical features, depth, precision, layer descriptors and tensor lengths, verified in results/m7-deployment-compatibility.json, and no allocation depends on weight values, so the computed request totals are byte-identical at 73,741,056 bytes. That is parity of what the application asks for. Actual device memory is unmeasured: identical requests do not exclude differences in driver or allocator behaviour, and no claim is made that the two models consume the same device memory.
